description:
`Bedrock.ObjectStorage.LocalFilesystem` writes objects in place. The S3 backend does not — one `put_object` (with `if_none_match: "*"` for the conditional case) is atomic, so an object is complete or absent. Readers are written against the S3 contract.

## 1. put_if_not_exists claims the key before filling it (worst)

lib/bedrock/object_storage/local_filesystem.ex:76-83

    case :file.open(path, [:write, :binary, :exclusive]) do
      {:ok, fd} ->
        try do
          :ok = :file.write(fd, data)

The exclusive create and the write are separate steps. Between them the key exists at zero length. A crash there claims the key permanently: every later attempt gets `:eexist` -> `{:error, :already_exists}`, and BOTH callers translate that to `:ok` — `Snapshot.write/3` (object_storage/snapshot.ex:82) and `put_chunk/2` (demux/shard_server.ex). Nothing can ever rewrite it.

This is the only writer for chunks and snapshots, and olivine/logic.ex already names the hazard for a different cause: "Snapshot.write's put-if-not-exists makes the poisoned bundle permanent."

## 2. put/4 truncates in place

`File.write(path, data)` at :29. A crash mid-write leaves an object part-old, part-new. Reachable via `put_if_version_matches/5`.

## 3. No fsync anywhere

Neither the file nor its parent directory is synced. A complete, correct write can vanish on power loss — and object storage is the durability substrate for the whole system.

## 4. Hard match on the write

`:ok = :file.write(fd, data)` raises MatchError on ENOSPC rather than returning an error, and leaves the exclusively-created key behind. A full disk permanently poisons the key being written.

## Detection is late and in the wrong shape

`Chunk.decode/1` (object_storage/chunk.ex:224-240) validates magic, header, and directory size but never checks the data section against the directory's extents. A tear past the directory decodes `{:ok, chunk}`; `extract_transactions/1` then raises ArgumentError from `binary_part/3` (chunk.ex:252) inside a materializer catch-up or a recovery replay — far from the write, and not the clean `{:error, :truncated_chunk}` the format returns elsewhere.

## Scope

Not dev-only despite the moduledoc: `cluster_supervisor.ex:241` makes LocalFilesystem the DEFAULT backend whenever `:object_storage` is unset.

## Fix

Write-temp-then-rename, in the same directory so the rename is atomic:
- `put/4`: write to `<key>.tmp.<unique>`, `:file.sync`, `:file.rename` over the target, then fsync the parent directory.
- `put_if_not_exists/4`: rename overwrites, so it cannot express create-only. Write and sync the temp, then `:file.make_link(tmp, path)` — which fails `:eexist` if the key exists — and unlink the temp either way. Link is atomic and gives exact exclusive-create semantics with a fully-formed file.
- return write errors instead of matching `:ok`, and unlink the temp on any failure so a partial write leaves nothing behind.
- consider validating the data section length in `Chunk.decode/1` so a truncated chunk is `{:error, :truncated_chunk}` rather than an ArgumentError at extraction.

## Test (write first, must fail)

- a temp/partial file left in the directory is never visible to `get/2` or `list/3`
- `put_if_not_exists` returns `{:error, :already_exists}` for a complete existing object, and succeeds where only a stale temp file exists
- a simulated write failure (ENOSPC via a tiny filesystem, or an injected fault) returns an error, leaves no key behind, and lets a retry succeed
- Chunk.decode of a chunk truncated inside the data section returns `{:error, :truncated_chunk}` rather than raising
title: [BUG] LocalFilesystem object writes are non-atomic and never fsynced; a torn put_if_not_exists is permanent
